insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 60 to 81 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Rain roughly matches crop needs
insights.body: Yearly rain and crop water demand are within about 225 mm of each other. Timing within the year matters more than the total.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Soybean, Groundnut and Cowpea score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: About 27 more scorching days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Days at 35 °C or hotter are heading from about 70 to 97 a year. Heat during flowering kills pollen, so grain and pod set drop — Soybean, Groundnut, Cowpea and Pigeon pea are most exposed.
consequences.action: Sow so flowering misses the hottest weeks, or pick heat-tolerant varieties.

consequences.headline: +1.0 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 27.3 °C to about 28.3 °C. That is close to the top of the comfortable range for Sweet potato.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 1,114 mm
consequences.detail: That is 18% below the 1,357 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.
